format_note: JSON, not YAML, so the guard stays stdlib-only and can run in every existing CI job without a pip install step.

scan.scan_scope_note: Only Python is scanned for violations. Markdown/config mentions are inventoried by hand in docs/repo-boundaries.md; they carry no import-time coupling.

skip_reasons.vllm: volatile upstream submodule; not ours to police
skip_reasons.vllm-ascend: volatile upstream submodule; not ours to police

scan.fixture_paths_note: This guard's own tests have to name cross-boundary paths as string fixtures to prove the guard detects them. Nothing else belongs here: a file that genuinely needs an exemption needs a baseline row instead, where it is dated and attributed to an extraction.
scan.module_search_paths_note: Directories that some entry point actually places on sys.path. Ownership of a derived module name is resolved from the owning file's path, so moving a file between subsystems moves its module with it. `.remote-dev` and `.agents/coordinator` are absent because both left this tree and are consumed as external checkouts.

ignored_modules.why: remote-dev ships an unrelated `mcp/` package. The extracted coordinator HTTP manager imports the installed MCP Python SDK, not that package. Treating `mcp` as substrate-owned would report a dependency that does not exist.
third-party ASGI dependency of the coordinator HTTP server

subsystems.summary: Stateless SSH-backed remote developer substrate. Must know nothing about vLLM-Ascend, sessions, or NPU leases.
subsystems.public_modules_note: The result contract and error taxonomy are schema-pinned (`schemas/result.schema.json` in the substrate) and remain the only import-level surface a consumer should bind to. The substrate additionally publishes the resolver plugin interface (`core.endpoint.register_resolver` / `resolver_setup` / `EndpointError`), which is how consumer selectors such as `machine` / `session_id` reach it. Because no substrate file is in this tree any more, these names are documentation for reviewers rather than something the guard can attribute.
subsystems.roots_note: No roots on `main`: the substrate left this tree with its extraction and is consumed as an external checkout (`.agents/deps/remote-dev.json`, `VAWS_REMOTE_DEV_ROOT`). Only consumers are in this repository: the resolver plugin `.agents/lib/vaws_remote_dev_plugin.py`, the launcher `.agents/scripts/remote_dev.py`, and the client configuration. The boundary is now a repository boundary, which is why this subsystem declares no paths.

subsystems.summary: Task identity, shared runtime pool, managed job supervision. Consumes remote-dev; must not consume the domain layer.
subsystems.roots_note: No roots on this tree: the coordinator left with its extraction and is consumed as an external checkout (`.agents/deps/coordinator.json`, `VAWS_COORDINATOR_ROOT`). Only consumers remain: `.agents/lib/vaws_coordinator.py`, `.agents/scripts/vaws.py`, `.agents/hooks/vaws_session.py`, and `.agents/scripts/vaws_client_setup.py`.
subsystems.public_modules_note: The task facade, stdio server and HTTP manager live in vaws-coordinator. This repository locates that checkout; it does not import those modules from an in-tree copy.

subsystems.summary: Loopback-only NPU fleet dashboard. Consumed as an external checkout of vllm-ascend-workspace/vaws-top; the scaffold consumer is `.agents/skills/npu-fleet-monitor/`.
subsystems.roots_note: No roots on `main`: the dashboard source is not in this tree. Only the bootstrap entry (`.agents/skills/npu-fleet-monitor/`) is, and that is a consumer.
subsystems.inline_patterns_note: A literal naming the dashboard as in-repo content — the `vaws-top` branch name handed to `git worktree add`, a direct local Path/open of the extracted skill, or a non-canonical URL. Only an entire exact supported GitHub HTTPS/SSH repository root, the owner/name repository identifier, or an exact published path descriptor is consumer reference, and a Path(...).read_text() of a local relative skill path remains a violation.
subsystems.published_external_references_note: Exact published surfaces of the extracted repository. A consumer may name an entire canonical GitHub URL, join one of these paths onto a located clone, or assign the descriptor. Substring `://`/`git@`, extra URL path, file URLs, mixed command strings, Path/open of the skill file, and Path(__file__)/ROOT joins that read that file are not exemptions.

subsystems.summary: The domain layer that stays: 24 skills, shared libraries, helper scripts. May depend on every extracted subsystem; none of them may depend on it.
subsystems.public_paths_note: Deliberately empty. The scaffold publishes nothing downward: a lower layer that needs scaffold data must receive it through an interface the lower layer owns, not read it.

subsystems.summary: Repository-level files: CI workflows, client config examples, top-level docs and shell helpers. Above every subsystem, so it may reference all of them.

rules.title: Dependencies point downward only
rules.why: The split exists because the substrate currently reaches backwards into scaffold-private state. A lower layer that imports a higher one cannot be extracted at all: `.remote-dev` would not build without `.agents/lib`, and `.agents/coordinator` would not build without the domain skills. Worse, remote-dev -> vaws_task_client -> coordinator -> core.endpoint closes a cycle across all three repos, so no extraction order exists until the cycle is cut. Every hit under this rule is a reverse dependency that must be inverted, not preserved.

rules.title: Cross-subsystem references target published entry points
rules.why: A downward dependency is fine; a downward dependency on someone else's internals is a version-pinning problem the moment the two live in different repositories. `.agents/coordinator/backend.py` reads `.remote-dev/core/managed_jobs.py` as *source text* and execs it on the remote host, which pins the coordinator to a byte-level detail of a file remote-dev is free to rewrite. Consumers must bind to the schema-pinned result contract and the CLI/MCP entry points instead.

rules.title: A domain skill uses another skill's published entry points only
rules.why: Skills are independently readable units; agents route to one by reading its SKILL.md. Reaching into a sibling's `scripts/` internals makes that routing a lie and couples two skills that a reader has no reason to read together. A referenced script counts as published when the owning skill's SKILL.md names it, which is exactly the contract an agent can discover.

rules.title: An extracted subsystem is not referenced as in-repo content
rules.why: `.agents/skills/npu-fleet-monitor/scripts/manage_monitor.py` used to locate the dashboard with `git worktree add <target> vaws-top` against this repository. After extraction the consumer must clone or locate the published vaws-top repository. Canonical GitHub URLs and the extracted skill/CLI paths are published consumer references, not in-repo content. Do not suppress remaining old branch/worktree routes through fixture exclusions or a blanket allowlist.
